paras: The killing of Arthur Harton took place near Curtis, Arkansas, in May 1888, when five Black men took Harton, a Black man, from his bed and beat him to death with an iron bar in a nearby thicket. Four of the five were arrested, and the papers that carried the story drew attention to the fact that three of the men were preachers. A later news summary said Harton had been accused of immorality.

According to a special dispatch to the Chicago Times from Arkadelphia, Harton was taken from his bed on Tuesday night, May 22, by five men, carried into the woods and murdered. A fuller account, attributed to Coroner Callow, placed the seizure on Tuesday morning and said the five "other negroes" carried him a short distance to a thicket, where his head was crushed with an iron bar. Callow had been summoned on Wednesday to sit on the body of a dead man near Curtis and identified it as Harton's.

The coroner's dispatch named the principals as George Dandridge, Willis Green, Bob Brogg, Anderson Mitchell and Dan Jones. A syndicated summary printed a week later gave the only stated reason for the attack, that Harton "had been accused of immorality."
All of the named men but one had been arrested by May 25, and the summary reported that the preachers were in jail. No report of an indictment, trial or sentence appears in the coverage.

The story reached the white press as two brief telegraphic items, a Chicago Times special printed by the Salt Lake Herald and the Sacramento Daily Record-Union on May 25, and the coroner's dispatch carried by the Waterbury Evening Democrat and the New York Sun on May 26. Headline writers made the preachers the point of the story, with "Murdered by Preachers" in Salt Lake, "Murdered by Negro Preachers" in Waterbury and "Deadly Work of Three Preachers" in the Sun. Every version called the five men murderers or principals and none described the killing as a lynching.

Weekly papers then ran the story as one paragraph in news-of-the-week columns, the Livingston Enterprise repeating the Chicago wire and the Middlebury Register and Willimantic Journal printing a rewritten version that added the accusation of immorality. The victim's name varied from paper to paper, appearing as Harton, Horton and Herton.

The accounts differ on when Harton was taken: the Chicago Times special said Tuesday night, the coroner's dispatch Tuesday morning, and the Willimantic Journal Thursday night. The Thursday date is inconsistent with the coroner's inquest on Wednesday and with the first dispatch, dated Thursday, May 24.

reader.title: Killing of Arthur Harton
bases: Five men took Harton from his bed at night and killed him in a thicket (A2, A3), and a later summary says he 'had been accused of immorality' (A5, A6), which presents the killing as a punishment carried out by a group.

Harton was killed by five men acting without any authority (A2, A3, A4), and a syndicated summary states he had been accused of immorality (A5, A6), a punitive pretext; the verdict is held at probable because the pretext appears only in that one summary text, while the two dispatches present the killing as murder by named individuals without stating a motive (A2, A3).

A Chicago Times special (A2) and a separate Arkadelphia dispatch based on the coroner (A3, A4) independently agree that five men took Harton from his bed and killed him and that three of those arrested were preachers.

accounts.label: Chicago Times special
accounts.gist: Harton, a negro, was taken from his bed Tuesday night by five men, carried into the woods and murdered; three of the arrested murderers were preachers.

accounts.label: Coroner's account (Arkadelphia dispatch)
accounts.gist: The coroner identified the body near Curtis as Arthur Horton, taken from bed Tuesday morning by five other negroes and killed with an iron bar in a thicket; five principals named, all arrested but one, three of them preachers.

accounts.label: Syndicated weekly summary
accounts.gist: Five negroes, three of them preachers, took Arthur Herton from his bed, crushed his head with an iron bar in a thicket; he had been accused of immorality and the preachers were in jail.

framing.detail: Brief wire items headed 'Murdered by Preachers' and 'Murdered by Negro Preachers' called the men 'murderers' and stressed that three were preachers.
The New York Sun headed the coroner dispatch 'Deadly Work of Three Preachers'; weekly summaries ran the story as one paragraph among unrelated news.

conflicts.note: Spelling variants of one name; the coroner dispatch (A3, A4) is the most direct source, but Harton is the spelling of the first report.

Thursday night cannot be right, since the coroner's inquest was held Wednesday and the first dispatch is dated Thursday, May 24 (A2, A4); 'Tuesday night' and 'Tuesday morning' may describe the same early hours.
